[BestTechAdvisor] @sachk: Anytime Fitness are exactly this brazen.
My mother was a member. When she died, I emailed Anytime Fitness to let them know. They continued to debit her account. I sent them the death certificate as proof and they ignored it, accumulating about $1.3k in fees then sold the debt onto a debt collection firm.
Luckily, the debt collection firm who bought the debt saw how ridiculous the situation was and immediately forgave the debt.
That's why I paid cash upfront instead of direct debit - and to avoid damaging my credit score - and Anytime Fitness still found a way to screw me over.
If you have one near you, Planet Fitness is better yet cheaper with no commitment. The only reason to sign up with Anytime Fitness is the number of locations in Australia. I hope franchisees jump ship though.
[HeyPapito] Or put $50-100 in an openrouter account and it will you will get 1.5+ years using the DeepSeek or Gemini models.

[JoeOz] You pay for what you use via API pricing on openrouter
You connect your API to the app of your choosing
[Homr] This doesn't work aswell as the native version. You have to setup system prompts, MCPs, servers etc etc. You have to have some decent knowledge if you want to mirror it 1:1
[schquid] @Homr: You can get a long way with the out of the box experience and asking it to replicate the features of $platform. Also start lean and add functionality when you notice an actual disparity. Loading up on skills, MCP and all the other bolt-ons before finding a feature gap will usually just eat context without necessarily improving your experience.
[TimeWaster] @Homr: Go to OpenRouter and make an account. Deposit maybe $10 to kind of activate your account and get some credits. (There’s a massive variety of free models on here but extended usage requires you to deposit and use some credit first). Then you need a harness. Probably the simplest one is HermesAgent which has a guided installer.
You’ll land with something similar to the chatGPT desktop app but with some functionality requiring setup (but it can help you through this and you can easily exceed the capabilities of the chat app once you’ve figured out your use case). Then you can setup external access through WhatsApp, Discord, Slack or iMessage.
This is about as simple as it gets (you could also just sign up to the free/paid subscription that the app tried to upsell to skip the OpenRouter step to get started). There’s YouTube videos to help as well. It’s a lot of fun and you’re really mostly limited by your imagination more so than usage limits. But I completely understand anyone who prefers a completely hands off approach for $$/month. Depends on your desire to tinker vs available time and income
[Homr] @TimeWaster: Thanks!! Interesting, I haven't heard of hermes agent before. I was thinking something completely different for the external app, something like openUI, chatbot, typingmind etc.
So is it possible to replicate native chatgpt plus using just the openrouter APIs?
[TimeWaster] @Homr: No worries! Rakazo is another one that might actually be better (basically a free version of GrokBot) but I haven’t personally used it to know. OpenUI will make it look like the ChatGPT website (fine if that’s all you need) but the desktop app is capable of a lot more (including building and running entire applications) which HermesAgent (or really any other harness) will help you to achieve that parity with ChatGPT app.
But once you really get into the weeds of it (especially if you start building apps like your own version of Xero, Woolies/Coles shopping, work roster, traffic checks, home automations, etc) then you’ll probably find that ChatGPT/Claude subscriptions are actually really good value and almost certainly sold at a loss.
